samples.reference: LiteParse is a standalone OSS PDF parsing tool focused exclusively on fast and light parsing.

samples.user_input: What is the parse speed per page using LiteParse?
samples.reference: LiteParse parses at an average of ~2-5ms per page.

samples.user_input: What platforms are supported by LiteParse?
samples.reference: LiteParse supports Linux, macOS (Intel/ARM), and Windows.

samples.user_input: What OCR engine does LiteParse use?
samples.reference: LiteParse uses the open source Tesseract OCR Engine, which requires zero setup and is bundled with the library.

samples.user_input: How do you install LiteParse for python?
samples.reference: To install LiteParse for python, run the command `pip install liteparse` in your terminal.

samples.user_input: What is the syntax for basic parsing with LiteParse?
samples.reference: For basic parsing with LiteParse, run the command: `lit parse document.pdf`.

samples.user_input: What is the syntax for parsing without OCR with LiteParse?
samples.reference: To parse without OCR with LiteParse, run the command: `lit parse document.pdf --no-ocr`.

samples.user_input: What languages does LiteParse currently support?
samples.reference: LiteParse currently supports Rust, Node.js/TypeScript, Python, or the browser (WASM).

samples.user_input: What tool does LiteParse use for spatial text parsing?
samples.reference: LiteParse uses PDFium for spatial text parsing.

samples.user_input: All package versions except for what language ship wit the same `lit` CLI in LiteParse?
samples.reference: All versions except for WASM ship with the same lit CLI.

samples.user_input: Can I use LiteParse as an agent skill?
samples.reference: Yes, you can use liteparse as an agent skill, downloading it with the skills CLI tool: `npx skills add run-llama/llamaparse-agent-skills --skill liteparse` or by copy-pasting the `SKILL.md` file to your own skills setup.

samples.user_input: How are images handled by LiteParse?
samples.reference: In LiteParse, image handling is controlled by the `--image-mode option`.

samples.user_input: Why is vector path output opt-in in LiteParse?
samples.reference: Vector path output is opt-in in LiteParse because path-heavy PDFs can produce large payloads.

samples.user_input: What document entries do parse results in LiteParse carry if present?
samples.reference: Parse results (Rust/Node/Python APIs) carry the document's `/Info`, `creator` and `producer` entries when present; these are API-only and never appear in CLI JSON output.

samples.user_input: How do you batch parse with LiteParse?
samples.reference: To parse an entire directory of documents with LiteParse, run the command: `lit batch-parse ./input-directory ./output-directory`.

samples.user_input: How do I screenshot all pages with LiteParse?
samples.reference: To screenshot all pages with LiteParse, run the command: `lit screenshot document.pdf -o ./screenshots`.

samples.user_input: What image formats does LiteParse natively support for automatic conversion to PDF before parsing?
samples.reference: LiteParse currently supports the following image formats: `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.bmp`, `.tiff`, `.webp`, and `.svg`.
